synthesis.headline: 50% of low-tech-comfort residents react negatively because they cannot decipher which blocks are included and fear hidden permit fees.

findings.claim: 50% of low-tech-comfort residents react negatively because they cannot decipher which blocks are included and fear hidden permit fees.
40% of sub-$25k households react negatively because extra permit fees feel unaffordable and the fee schedule is hidden.
35% of high-skepticism readers react negatively because the notice hides the fee schedule and cites no traffic-study proof.

highest_leverage_edit.current_text: fee schedule maintained by the Department of Transportation and published separately on the City's website
highest_leverage_edit.proposed_text: flat fee of $15 per additional permit and $5 per visitor pass, frozen for two years
highest_leverage_edit.rationale: Publishing a fixed fee inline removes the trust barrier.

synthesis.who_you_are_losing: Low-tech-comfort, low-income, and high-skepticism residents who cannot navigate hidden fee lookups, opaque block maps, and paperwork hassles.
synthesis.who_you_are_winning: High-tech-comfort residents in Southeast and West US who ignore city notices unless their exact street is named.
